# Cardiovascular Fitness for a 42-Year-Old Beginner

For a beginner who is **12 kg overweight**, has **mild asthma**, and wants to protect the **knees**, both running and brisk walking can improve fitness over 12 weeks. The safest place to start is usually **brisk walking**, then progress only if symptoms and joints stay calm.

## Running vs. Brisk Walking: What Fits Best

| Option | Pros | Cons | Knee Load | Asthma Consideration | Best Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Running | Faster cardio gains; time-efficient; strong fitness stimulus | Higher impact; more knee stress; harder to recover from; can trigger breathing symptoms sooner | High | More likely to provoke symptoms if intensity rises too fast | Later-stage progression if walking feels easy |
| Brisk walking | Lower impact; easier to control breathing; more joint-friendly; easier to sustain consistently | Slower fitness gains; may need longer sessions for same cardio effect | Low | Usually easier to manage with warm-up and pacing | Best starting point for most beginners |

## 12-Week Progression Plan

### Brisk Walking Progression
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Weeks 1-2:** 20-30 minutes, 4 days/week, easy-to-brisk pace; finish feeling you could do more.
- **Weeks 3-4:** 30-35 minutes, 4-5 days/week; add 5 x 1-minute faster segments.
- **Weeks 5-6:** 35-40 minutes, 5 days/week; include 8 x 1-minute brisk intervals.
- **Weeks 7-8:** 40-45 minutes, 5 days/week; one session can become a hill or incline walk if knees tolerate it.
- **Weeks 9-10:** 45 minutes, 5 days/week; 10 x 1-minute brisk intervals or 2 x 8-minute steady efforts.
- **Weeks 11-12:** 45-60 minutes, 5 days/week; maintain a pace that raises breathing but still allows short sentences.

### Running Progression
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg
- **Weeks 1-2:** 1 minute jog + 2-3 minutes walk, repeated for 20 minutes, 2-3 days/week.
- **Weeks 3-4:** 90 seconds jog + 2 minutes walk, repeated for 20-25 minutes, 2-3 days/week.
- **Weeks 5-6:** 2 minutes jog + 2 minutes walk, repeated for 24-30 minutes, 2-3 days/week.
- **Weeks 7-8:** 3 minutes jog + 90 seconds walk, repeated for 25-30 minutes, 3 days/week.
- **Weeks 9-10:** 5 minutes jog + 2 minutes walk, repeated for 30-35 minutes, 3 days/week.
- **Weeks 11-12:** 10-15 minutes continuous easy jog only if knees, breathing, and recovery are all stable.

## Safer Starting Choice

**Recommendation: start with brisk walking.**

Why it is safer:
- Lower impact is better for **overweight beginners** and **knee protection**.
- Easier to keep intensity in a range that is less likely to trigger **asthma symptoms**.
- Builds a base of consistency, which matters more than speed for the first 12 weeks.

When running becomes reasonable:
- Walking feels easy at a moderate pace.
- No knee pain during or after sessions.
- No wheezing, chest tightness, or unusual breathlessness with brisk walking.
- You can tolerate 45-60 minutes of walking comfortably.

## Knee- and Asthma-Friendly Rules

- Use a **5-10 minute warm-up** every session.
- Keep effort at a level where you can speak in short phrases.
- Stop or scale back if knee pain rises above mild discomfort or lasts into the next day.
- Avoid hard surfaces and worn-out shoes.
- For asthma, choose cooler, less polluted times of day and keep your rescue inhaler available if prescribed.
